title: Catalogue Orders Paid From a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card
content:
A member may spend the allowance by ordering from the plan's catalogue, and the value of the items and the delivery charge come off the card when the order is placed. These are the terms on which a catalogue order is taken against a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card.

**The order and its charges.** An order must reach the tier's order minimum before the plan will process it, and the delivery charge depends on the service chosen; expedited delivery costs the tier's expedited fee whatever the order is worth.

**Cancelling an order.** *The two clauses that follow are no longer in force and have been superseded by the current basis:* "The member asks for the order to be cancelled no later than the cancellation deadline counted from the time the order was placed." "Hours are counted as full 24-hour periods from the moment the order was placed, a request made exactly on the deadline is in time, and calendar days are never used in place of hours."

After that deadline the order may still be cancelled while it has not shipped, but the delivery charge is not returned, because the plan has already paid for the despatch.

**The delivery date.** The plan quotes a delivery date from the tier's processing days and the shipping days of the service chosen, counted in business days, and tells the member that date when the order is taken.

**An item the plan cannot fill.** Where the plan cannot fill an item the whole order is cancelled and every penny, including the delivery charge, goes back on the card in the benefit period it came from.

**An order that has not arrived.** An order the member has not got can be traced by its tracking reference, and a delivery the carrier shows as made is re-sent once rather than argued over.

superseded_clauses: The member asks for the order to be cancelled no later than the cancellation deadline counted from the time the order was placed.
Hours are counted as full 24-hour periods from the moment the order was placed, a request made exactly on the deadline is in time, and calendar days are never used in place of hours.
